indigo-navy.$description: Indigo Navy — Primary brand color — filled CTAs, navigation active states, heading text, logo wordmark. The deep violet-tinted navy carries institutional weight without going pure black; pairs with white text for the site's most confident button

midnight-ink.$description: Midnight Ink — Dark surface and emphasis text — product card backgrounds, high-contrast body copy. Near-gray with a cool blue-green undertone; works as the dark-mode substrate when a section needs to invert

slate-ink.$description: Slate Ink — Secondary heading and body text — slightly warmer than Midnight Ink, used where pure black feels too harsh against the light canvas

steel.$description: Steel — Body and link text — the dominant muted text color (245 occurrences in body). Neutral gray-blue that reads as quiet, never washed out

fog.$description: Fog — Icon strokes, tertiary borders, placeholder text. Mid-gray that separates without competing with text

mist.$description: Mist — Lightest body text — captions, disclaimers, fine print. Stays legible on white but recedes visually

silver-lining.$description: Silver Lining — Card borders, input borders, divider lines. The structural hairline color — appears wherever two surfaces need to separate without shadow

cloud-canvas.$description: Cloud Canvas — Page background — the dominant canvas color. Near-white with a barely-perceptible cool tint that keeps the page from feeling sterile

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Card surfaces, nav background, button fills, secondary text. The top layer of the surface stack

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Nav icons, dark icon strokes — slightly bluer than pure black, used in icon contexts where Slate Ink would be too warm

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Deep icon strokes and nav elements. Near-black with a blue undertone that matches the indigo navy family

pure-black.$description: Pure Black — Maximum contrast text, dark fills in illustrations. Used sparingly — Indigo Navy or Slate Ink carry most text work

signal-orange.$description: Signal Orange — Accent CTA fill and featured card background — one of the few saturated warm colors in the system. Appears on the Brex highlight card and select buttons to draw the eye without feeling decorative

peach-glow.$description: Peach Glow — Soft accent surface — lighter companion to Signal Orange, used as card backgrounds where warmth is needed at lower intensity

seafoam-600.$description: Seafoam 600 — Code and data text — the signature color for JSON keys, identifiers, and financial values in code snippets. Also used for chart data points and growth visualizations

seafoam-700.$description: Seafoam 700 — Darker seafoam for strokes, chart lines, and icon accents in data contexts. Anchors the seafoam scale on darker backgrounds

seafoam-400.$description: Seafoam 400 — Highlighted code text — string values, URLs, API endpoints in code blocks. The lightest seafoam, reads as green-tinted monospace

deep-sea.$description: Deep Sea — Decorative stroke and chart accent — deep teal used in SVG illustrations and data visualizations alongside the seafoam scale

sky-cyan.$description: Sky Cyan — Soft accent surface and stroke — appears as background washes behind data widgets and as decorative chart strokes

cobalt-edge.$description: Cobalt Edge — Violet wash for highlight backgrounds, decorative bands, and soft emphasis behind content. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

ocean-depth.$description: Ocean Depth — Decorative fill — medium blue used in illustration and SVG contexts

suisseintl.$description: Primary typeface — used for all headings, body, buttons, nav, links, and card text. The custom geometric grotesque gives Column a distinctive editorial register that distinguishes it from Inter-only fintechs. Weight 600 at 52–60px for display, weight 500 for sub-headings, weight 400 for body, weight 300 for low-emphasis links.

suisseintlmono.$description: Monospace companion to SuisseIntl — used for technical labels, API identifiers, and inline data in UI chrome. Maintains the same proportions as SuisseIntl so mono and proportional text align cleanly in mixed contexts.

sfmono.$description: Code snippet rendering — appears in JSON examples and API documentation blocks. Tinted in seafoam green scale to visually distinguish code from UI prose.

inter.$description: UI fallback font — used in dashboard and product surface contexts where Inter's wider character set and system familiarity take priority over brand identity.
